options.content:
Computing is a major contributor to energy consumption, and thus is one of the main sources of the carbon emission of our research. In the context of the global climate crisis, it is imperative that individuals and organizations find ways to assess, then reduce, the carbon footprint of their work. This page aims to represent the carbon footprint that we are, collectively and individually, responsible for at the institution. SLURM jobs submitted to High Performance Clusters are logged automatically (including information such as resource requested, run time, memory efficiency, etc.), and the corresponding carbon footprint was calculated using the framework proposed by Green Algorithms.

We built this tool in the hope of raising awareness of computing usage, highlighting resource waste, and fostering good computing practices. This is intended to be a lightweight carbon footprint calculator, not a cluster monitoring system.

Report for user $user_name

Find out your carbon footprint for the time period selected (see date panel at top).

SELECT a.submitdate, SUM(a.carbonfootprint) FROM (SELECT d.submitdate, d.carbonfootprint FROM ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d ON u.user_name = d.user_name WHERE u.user_name = '${__user.login}') AS a GROUP BY a.submitdate ORDER BY a.submitdate ASC

Successful vs Failed Jobs (user $user_name)

Because any resource spent on a job is wasted if the job fails, it is important to test scripts and pipelines on small datasets. The chart below shows the daily success and failure rates of jobs that completed in the time period selected (see date panel at top).

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(n_jobs) AS "No. of jobs completed", to_char(SUM(carbonfootprint_failedjobs)/1000,'99999999.99') AS "Failed jobs' footprint (kgCO2e)", to_char(SUM(cost_failedjobs), '9999999') AS "Cost of failed jobs", to_char((SUM(n_jobs-n_success)::float/SUM(n_jobs))*100, '999.99') AS "% of failed jobs" FROM ga_data_aggregate WHERE user_name = '${__user.login}' AND $__timeFilter(submitdate);

custom.axisLabel: Carbon footprint of failed jobs (in red)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  submitdate,
  SUM(carbonfootprint_failedjobs) AS "Failed jobs",
  SUM(carbonfootprint-carbonfootprint_failedjobs) AS "Successful jobs"
FROM
  ga_data_aggregate
WHERE
  user_name = '${__user.login}'
GROUP BY
  submitdate
ORDER BY
  submitdate ASC;

options.content:
Memory efficiency (user $user_name)

Memory can be a significant source of waste, because the power draw from memory mainly depends on the memory available, not on the actual memory used. The chart below shows the distribution of the memory efficiency (the closer to 100% the better) collected from all this user's jobs in the period chosen (see date panel at top)..

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.range as "Memory efficiency (%)", SUM(n_jobs) as "Number of jobs"
from 
(
    select '0-4' as range, 4 as endrange
        union all select '5-9', 9
        union all select '10-14', 14
        union all select '15-19', 19
        union all select '20-24', 24
        union all select '25-29', 29
        union all select '30-34', 34
        union all select '35-39', 39
        union all select '40-44', 44
        union all select '45-49', 49
        union all select '50-54', 54
        union all select '55-59', 59
        union all select '60-64', 64
        union all select '65-69', 69
        union all select '70-74', 74
        union all select '75-79', 79
        union all select '80-84', 84
        union all select '85-89', 89
        union all select '90-94', 94
        union all select '95-99', 99
        union all select '100', 100
) as r
left join ga_data_aggregate on 
r.endrange = case 
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) = 100 then 100
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 95 then 99
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 90 then 94
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 85 then 89
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 80 then 84
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 75 then 79
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 70 then 74
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 65 then 69
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 60 then 64
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 55 then 59
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 50 then 54
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 45 then 49
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 40 then 44
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 35 then 39
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 30 then 34
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 25 then 29
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 20 then 24
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 15 then 19
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 10 then 14
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 5 then 9
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) >= 0 then 4
    end
    WHERE user_name='${__user.login}' AND $__timeFilter(submitdate)
    group by r.range, r.endrange order by r.endrange;

options.content:
Carbon footprint for the users in your group ($group_name)

Carbon footprint of all users in your group ($group_name) in the time range specified.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.submitdate, SUM(a.carbonfootprint) AS "Carbon footprint of", a.name
FROM
(SELECT d.submitdate, u.name, d.carbonfootprint FROM ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d ON u.user_name = d.user_name WHERE u.group_name = '$group_name') AS a
GROUP BY
a.submitdate, a.name;

panels.title: Carbon footprints of users in your group ($group_name)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.user_name AS "Username", a.name AS "Name", to_char(SUM(carbonfootprint)/1000, '9999999') AS "Carbon footprint (kgCO2e)", to_char(SUM(a.cost), '9999') AS "Cost"
FROM
(SELECT u.user_name, u.name, d.carbonfootprint, d.cost FROM ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d ON u.user_name = d.user_name WHERE u.group_name = '$group_name' AND $__timeFilter(d.submitdate)) AS a
GROUP BY a.user_name, a.name
ORDER BY a.user_name;

panels.title: Contribution of users to the carbon footprint of your group ($group_name)
